title: Sort activates the query adapter and renders in the announced direction
description: Column headers advertise sortability via a keyboard-reachable sort control; activation flips direction (asc / desc), announces the new direction through `aria-sort`, and reorders rendered rows to match the server-side sort (TAC-1802) when the project chose the server-side default. The client-side sort alternative applies to small in-memory collections when the operator elicited it (ADR-1802's elicited alternative). The recommended default `url-state-strategy` is `url-query`: the shell serialises `sort`, `q` and `page` into the URL query on every state change via `history.replaceState`. The elicited alternative `session-scoped` keeps the same state in memory for the shell mount lifetime and suppresses URL writes (ADR-1802).
rationale: Sort is the single-most-used interaction on a datatable and the most common source of hidden accessibility regressions. Anchoring the direction announcement and the keyboard reach at the surface level closes both.
